 Can Altria's 64.5% Smokeable Margin Sustain Profit Growth Ahead?

 TPB -19.16%

 Learn more Altria Group, Inc. MO continued to deliver strong profitability in the smokeable products segment in the third quarter of 2026, supported by higher pricing and increased refunds of taxes and duties paid on imported cigarettes. The segment's adjusted operating companies income ("OCI") margin reached 64.5%, up from 64.4% a year earlier. This improvement came despite lower cigarette shipments, increased promotional spending and higher manufacturing costs.
Adjusted OCI rose 3.9% year over year to $3.07 billion, while revenues net of excise taxes increased 3.7% to $4.76 billion. Price realization stood at 4.4%, reflecting the impact of Marlboro Cowboy Cut and Basic volume growth on the sales mix. Marlboro strengthened its premium position, with share reaching 60%, while Basic continued to gain ground in the discount category. The company's portfolio approach across different price points remains particularly relevant amid continued economic pressure on adult smokers.
However, declining cigarette demand remains a challenge. Reported domestic cigarette shipments fell 2.9% in the quarter. Adjusting for trade inventory movements, estimated cigarette volumes declined 4%, compared with an estimated 5% drop for the industry. Higher promotional investments, a greater mix of discount shipments and increased manufacturing costs also partly offset the benefits from pricing and tax and duty refunds.
For the first nine months of 2026, smokeable adjusted OCI grew 4.1% to $8.77 billion, with the adjusted margin expanding 0.4 percentage points to 64.8%. Continued pricing strength and tax and duty refunds remain important to sustaining smokeable profitability amid declining cigarette volumes, an unfavorable sales mix and higher manufacturing costs. 
 Altria and Industry Peers Navigate Evolving Margin Trends 
 Philip Morris International Inc. PM delivered strong profitability in the international combustibles segment in the third quarter of 2026. Supported by 8.9% pricing and broadly flat cigarette shipments, Philip Morris reported 9.8% organic gross profit growth. The segment's adjusted gross margin expanded 130 basis points to 68.5%. Philip Morris benefited from strong pricing and market share gains despite unfavorable geographic mix and higher costs.
 Turning Point Brands, Inc. TPB reported a 56.9% adjusted gross margin in the Stoker's segment for second-quarter 2026, down from 62.5% a year earlier amid higher chain penetration. Driven by favorable product mix, Turning Point Brands recorded a 57.3% adjusted gross margin at Zig-Zag, up from 49.1%. Turning Point Brands faces profitability pressure from increased sales and marketing investments despite strong Modern Oral growth. 
 Story Continues Altria's Price Performance, Valuation & Estimates 
 Shares of Altria have gained 16.2% in the past three months compared with the industry's growth of 8.5%. 
 Zacks Investment Research Image Source: Zacks Investment Research 
 From a valuation standpoint, MO trades at a forward price-to-earnings ratio of 12.99X, down from the industry's average of 16.28X. 
 Zacks Investment Research Image Source: Zacks Investment Research 
 The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MO's 2026 and 2027 earnings implies year-over-year growth of 5.2% and 3.3%, respectively.
